literal: Forgetting anger towards anyone; evil things arising because of that will come.
translation: One should forget anger towards anyone whomsoever, for all evil things arise because of it.
modern: யாரிடத்திலும் கோபம் கொள்வதை மறந்துவிட வேண்டும்; ஏனென்றால், தீமைகள் அனைத்தும் அந்தக் கோபத்தினாலேயே உண்டாகும்.
explanation: This couplet explains why we must completely avoid anger. The word 'மறத்தல்' literally means forgetting, but here it carries the sense of completely letting go or abandoning. We must do this 'யார்மாட்டும்'—towards anyone, regardless of their status or how they treat us. The second line warns that 'தீய' (evil consequences and pain) will 'பிறத்தல்' (arise) 'அதனான்' (because of that anger). Thus, by showing that anger is the sole source of harmful outcomes, the poet urges us to eliminate it entirely.
